stem:
Fig. 10.1 shows a simple laminated iron-core transformer consisting of a primary coil of 2500 turns and a secondary coil of 625 turns.

[[fig:f1]]

The output potential difference (p.d.) *V*₍OUT₎ is applied to a load resistor of resistance 640 Ω.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State the function of the iron core.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why the iron core is laminated.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead: The input p.d. *V*₍IN₎ is a sinusoidal alternating voltage of peak value 12 kV and period 40 ms.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the root-mean-square (r.m.s.) current in the load resistor.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
On Fig. 10.2, sketch the variation with time *t* of the power *P* dissipated in the load resistor for time *t* = 0 to *t* = 40 ms. Assume that *P* = 0 when *t* = 0.

[[fig:f2]]

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain, with reference to Fig. 10.2, why the mean power in the load resistor is 70 W.

figures.caption: Fig. 10.1
figures.alt: A laminated iron-core transformer with primary and secondary coils, an alternating input voltage, and a 640 Ω load resistor across the output.

figures.caption: Fig. 10.2
figures.alt: A blank power-versus-time graph with a grid, time axis from 0 to 40 ms, and power axis from −200 W to 200 W.
